title: Turing's First Imitation Game: Design Concepts and a Human-Approximates-Machine Reading
abstract: arXiv:2608.05558v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This paper examines Turing's 1948 report, "Intelligent Machinery", as an important conceptual source for the later imitation games. Its first contribution is to identify and integrate the design concepts underlying the 1948 chess-based imitation game: the possibility that intelligent machines may make mistakes, the exclusion of irrelevant physical features, the role of the human judge, and Turing's claim that intellectual activity consists mainly of search. The paper's second contribution is to argue that restricting the human contestant to a rather poor chess player increases the role of intellectual search and makes human behaviour more comparable to machine behaviour. This interpretation presents the 1948 game as a human-approximates-machine game and suggests that the imitation game framework can be used not only to ask whether machines imitate humans, but also to examine when human intelligence becomes machine-like under sp

translated_title: 图灵的第一个模仿游戏：设计概念与“人类近似机器”的解读
translated_abstract: 本文考察了图灵1948年的报告《智能机器》，将其视为后来模仿游戏的重要概念来源。本文的第一项贡献是识别并整合了1948年基于国际象棋的模仿游戏背后的设计概念：智能机器可能犯错的可能性、对无关物理特征的排除、人类裁判的角色，以及图灵关于智力活动主要由搜索构成的主张。本文的第二项贡献是论证将人类参赛者限制为一名相当差劲的国际象棋选手，会增加智力搜索的作用，并使人类行为与机器行为更具可比性。这一解读将1948年的游戏呈现为一个“人类近似机器”的游戏，并表明模仿游戏框架不仅可用于探究机器是否能够模仿人类，还可用于考察在何种条件下人类智能会变得类似机器。
tldr: 本文通过分析图灵1948年的《智能机器》报告，识别出其基于国际象棋的模仿游戏的核心设计概念，并提出将人类选手设定为差劲棋手使该游戏成为“人类近似机器”的游戏，从而拓展了模仿游戏框架的用途。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the design concepts underlying Turing's 1948 chess-based imitation game in his "Intelligent Machinery" report, and argues that restricting the human contestant to a poor chess player transforms it into a human-approximates-machine game, extending the imitation game framework beyond asking whether machines imitate humans.
